title: Interference, phase and coherence mark scheme

questions.answer: The spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle.

marking_points.text: States that diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle

option_feedback.A: Coherence does not require equal amplitudes.
option_feedback.B: Zero phase difference is one possible constant phase difference, not the only one.
option_feedback.D: Direction of travel does not define coherence.

marking_points.text: Selects C, the waves have a constant phase difference

option_feedback.B: Equal opposite displacements cancel rather than leave one amplitude.
option_feedback.C: Doubling occurs for equal waves in phase.
option_feedback.D: Amplitude addition cannot give four times one amplitude for two equal waves.

marking_points.text: Selects A, equal antiphase waves have zero resultant amplitude

option_feedback.A: Zero path difference keeps waves in phase.
option_feedback.B: One wavelength returns waves to the same phase.
option_feedback.C: Two wavelengths returns waves to the same phase.

marking_points.text: Selects D, a path difference of 2.5λ
Calculates the path difference as 35 cm - 26 cm = 9.0 cm

parts.answer: Destructive interference occurs because 1.5λ is an odd half-wavelength path difference, so equal waves from the in-phase sources arrive in antiphase and cancel.

marking_points.text: Explains that 1.5λ is an odd half-wavelength path difference so equal waves arrive in antiphase and cancel
Adds the two amplitudes because the waves arrive in phase

parts.answer: 1.5 mm. At 180° the signed displacements oppose, so the resultant amplitude is |3.5 - 2.0| mm. Cancellation is incomplete because the amplitudes are unequal.

marking_points.text: Subtracts the amplitudes because the waves are in antiphase
Explains that unequal amplitudes cannot cancel completely

parts.answer: At t1: +3.0 mm; at t2: 0 mm; at t3: -3.0 mm.

marking_points.text: Adds +2.0 mm and +1.0 mm to obtain +3.0 mm at t1
Adds zero and zero to obtain zero displacement at t2
Adds -2.0 mm and -1.0 mm to obtain -3.0 mm at t3

parts.answer: The separate phase-marker waves are not coherent because their phase difference changes with time.

marking_points.text: States that the separate phase-marker waves are not coherent
Explains that their phase difference changes with time rather than remaining constant

parts.answer: Superposition is an instantaneous displacement-adding rule, so the individual signed displacements can be added whenever waves overlap even if their relative phase later changes.

marking_points.text: Explains that superposition adds instantaneous signed displacements whenever waves overlap and does not require coherence
